newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Cenbank to tighten money policy - Petkoff.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Cenbank to tighten money policy - Petkoff.

text.p: Venezuela's Central Bank will tighten its monetary policy with larger bond issues in an effort to fend off inflationary pressure stemming from due public sector wage rises, Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said.
"The Central Bank has to apply a tight money policy as the coming wage increases imply a considerable expansion in public spending and money in circulation," Petkoff told reporters.
Wages among Venezuela's 1.2 million public sector workers are due to rise 70 percent under a February pay agreement the government has not yet met.
Petkoff said the Bank would soon be able to count on a long awaited tranche of treasury bills among its arsenal of monetary weapons -- and not just Central Bank TEMs.

"The government's 400 billion bolivars bond issue to the Bank is on the point of being approved, and there may be more than that," Petkoff said. The bonds, which will be used to pay-off government debt with the Central Bank, will be used in open market operations alongside Central Bank TEMs.

Petkoff said that Treasury Letters may also be used, and pending external debt payments would act "like a mechanism for destroying money." He added that rising imports would also help reduce excess liquidity in the economy.
